clue.text: Decide heartless exploit calls for a beating

parts.note: an exploit is a daring deed or feat

explanation.definitionFit: A defeat is a beating in the sense of a loss suffered in a contest.

clue.text: Elevated piece of nonsense — medieval house and grounds

indicators.note: Elevated says the hidden letters are read backwards
piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some lofty bit of medieval nonsense about a manor and its estate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Elevated' means read upwards: the run ENSEMED inside 'nonsense — medieval' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is the land attached to a manor, kept for the lord's own use: a house with its estate.

clue.text: Home in autumn, almost non-negotiable

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
being in is being at home

explanation.surface: A homeowner's autumn deal is very nearly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something final is settled and closed, so it is no longer open to negotiation.

clue.text: Religious lady's short reply about housework

indicators.note: about puts the shortened reply round the other piece
short trims the word for reply down to its first three letters

parts.note: a reply is an answer
household chores are housework

explanation.surface: A pious woman's curt response to being asked about the cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious lady's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is only a link; 'short' leaves ANS, which 'about' wraps round the housework.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoress is a woman who withdraws from the world to live a religious life in seclusion.

clue.text: Show total return by one state

indicators.note: return makes the word for total run backwards

parts.note: a total is a sum
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A presentation of the full tally given out by a single region.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical is a stage show built around songs.

clue.text: Ascetic Scotsman confused Sikh

indicators.note: confused says the letters of Sikh are jumbled

explanation.surface: A self-denying Scot mistook someone for a Sikh.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkish means like a monk, and monks are known for an austere, self-denying life.

clue.text: Ornament shoots up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to shoot a gun is to fire it, so shoots gives fires

explanation.surface: A decorative flourish springs upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small decorative stroke finishing a letter in many typefaces.

clue.text: Joint lead in charge of a country

parts.note: a co-star shares the leading role in a film or play

explanation.surface: Two actors sharing top billing take charge of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a country in Central America.

explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for 'that is', abbreviated IE, which is removed from LINGERIE.

clue.text: The gnarled tree in protective cover

parts.note: an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A twisted old tree serving as a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnarled' looks like it describes the tree, but it twists 'The' into HET, and 'in' sets the tree inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is a hard covering worn to protect the head.

clue.text: Crazed male, an upholder of heresy

parts.note: crazed means wildly frantic, manic

explanation.definitionFit: A Manichean follows Manichaeism, a dualist religion condemned by the Church as heretical.

clue.text: Second check round for plant extract

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A further inspection for something taken from a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky substance that oozes from certain trees and plants.

clue.text: Origins of short and long vowels obvious in salute

explanation.surface: Advice on pronouncing vowels clearly in a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous firing of guns, often as a salute.

clue.text: Nattered endlessly, being moved to beg

explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts Nattered to NATTERE, and 'being moved' rearranges those letters.

clue.text: Bully from the hills holding hands

explanation.surface: A thug coming down from the hills clutching hands.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor; the two tors hold MEN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor torments others, as a bully does.

clue.text: Man's eating a horse on a full stomach!

parts.note: his is the possessive of a man
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.walkthrough: Haggis is a Scottish dish of offal and oatmeal traditionally cooked in a sheep's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggis is literally a sheep's stomach stuffed tight with a filling.

clue.text: Had to forget about the underworld boss

clue.text: Dramatic moment when converted Catholic is reproduced

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a decisive turning point, a dramatic moment.

clue.text: Sequence of notes involving piano and lute — head surgeon's instrument

parts.note: a scale is a sequence of notes
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of lute

explanation.surface: A musical line on piano and lute for a leading surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks attached to surgeon but takes the first letter of 'lute'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is the small sharp knife a surgeon cuts with.

clue.text: Animal swallowing bits of dog food, unable to get up

indicators.note: swallowing places the picked letters inside the animal

parts.note: a beast is an animal

indicators.note: bits of takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A creature gulps down dog food and cannot stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfast is an old word for bedridden, confined to bed.

clue.text: Appearance after drinking too much distilled barley?

indicators.note: distilled spirit is made by processing grain, so the letters are worked into new form

explanation.surface: How you look after too much whisky made from barley.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and blurred, the typical look of someone hungover.

clue.text: Frame funny letters

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Joke messages put someone in the frame.

clue.text: Cold drink dispenser from Egypt

clue.text: Exaggerate: "Queen Street split like an egg!"

clue.text: Huddled mass of low-lifers bearing right

clue.text: Contend a herb carries little weight

clue.text: Insatiable appetite for g-grass

parts.note: the stammered g is taken as a letter in its own right
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A stammering confession of a craving for grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is a hunger for more than one needs.

clue.text: Coach at front of train in reversal of 1 across

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside
reversal of reads the synonym backwards

parts.note: the answer to 1 across means a beating, and a rout is a heavy defeat

indicators.note: at front of takes the opening letter of train

clue.text: On which to write role involving churchmen

clue.text: Sweet beast sheltering artist

clue.text: Traverse black spine
